sources.entry: Localization Editor - Simple macOS editor app to help you manage iOS app localizations by allowing you to edit all the translations side by side.

summary.one_liner: A simple macOS app for viewing and editing iOS Localizable.strings files side by side, highlighting missing translations.
summary.what_it_does: Opens a folder chosen via File | Open folder, finds all Localizable.strings files, and detects each file's language. It shows all translations in one view with keys sorted in the first column and each language as a column, so translations can be compared. Missing translations in any language are visible. Editing a translation writes the change back to the corresponding Localizable.strings file. The README notes that pointing it at a whole project root works but takes longer to process.
use_cases: Edit iOS localization strings in a table
Manage translations for an iOS or macOS app
Check which strings lack a translation
how_to_run: Or download LocalizationEditor.app.zip from the latest GitHub release
Right-click LocalizationEditor.app and choose Open the first time (double-click shows a warning because the app is signed only with a development certificate)
In the app, choose File | Open folder with localization files and select your localization folder
stack: Swift (implied by Xcode-style app; not explicitly named in README)
notable: Side-by-side view of all languages with keys sorted in the first column
Writes edits back to the Localizable.strings files
Available in English and Chinese UI
caveats: Pointing it at a whole project root is slower to process
The release build is signed only with a development certificate, so Gatekeeper needs a right-click open
